MethodSummary

static escapeForMessage(string $value): stringQuoted single-line repr of $value for exception messages. Printable ASCII passes through (with quote/backslash escapes and \n \r \t); every other byte becomes \xHH. var_export() and print_r() re-emit control and UTF-8 bytes raw into the message, so a hostile id could smuggle terminal traffic into every log or terminal that later prints the refusal. This function escapes everything that is not printable ASCII instead.

ZoneClickTracker final class

Deduplicate press/release pairs so callers receive one ClickResult per logical click — suppressing spurious extra Press events fired during a drag and discarding mismatched Press+Release pairs on different zones.

MethodSummary
static new(): selfHouse ::new() factory - same signature as the public constructor, which stays public for BC (SM-S31, gate G12 house-convention half).
track(MouseEvent $event, ?Zone $hitZone = null): ?ClickResultFeed a mouse event and receive a ClickResult if the event completes a clean Press+Release pair on the same zone.
observeRelease(MouseEvent $event, ?Zone $hitZone = null): boolRead-only view of the release-agreement gate: would a track() call with THIS release event and re-hit zone complete the click? Answers without consuming the pending press. A caller can distinguish "I forgot to re-resolve" (false with null, true once passed the fresh hit) from "the zone genuinely moved" (false either way). The silent null from track() cannot tell those apart, and misclick-protection consumers want to know which one they hit.
setPressZone(Zone $zone, int $button): voidInject the zone that was hit at the time of the press event. Call this immediately after track(Press) when you have the zone. The Release call must still carry the fresh re-hit zone for the Release-agreement gate — setPressZone() only stores the press half.

Manager final class

Mouse-zone manager. Wraps content with sentinel-tagged zone markers identifying a logical "zone". scan() later finds those markers, records each zone's bounding box in terminal cells, and returns the cleaned-up frame.

MethodSummary
__construct()Public for BC; newUnprefixed() is the house spelling.
static newUnprefixed(): selfBuild a fresh un-prefixed manager, independent of every other instance. The name says what it builds: a manager with NO id prefix. Distinct from the Zones facade's shared default manager (Zones::defaultManager()) — use that one only when the whole program agrees on a single zone namespace.
static newGlobal(): self
static newPrefix(string $prefix = ''): selfBuild a manager that namespaces every id with a unique prefix.
static newWithIdPrefix(string $prefix): selfA manager stamping exactly $prefix onto every id, with no counter bookkeeping — the raw constructor ZoneRegistry::newPrefix() builds on. An empty prefix builds an un-prefixed manager. Prefer newPrefix() (or a registry's) unless the prefix is already known to be unique.
setEnabled(bool $on): voidToggle marker emission and scanning. When $enabled = false, mark() returns $content verbatim (no markers wrapped — but the id is STILL validated, so flipping the manager off must not become a way to smuggle an illegal id through the emit path) and scan() is a no-op pass-through. Useful for non-interactive output (CI logs, file dumps) where the markers add nothing.
isEnabled(): bool
motionTrackingAnsi(bool $on): stringBuild the all-motion tracking byte sequence — RETURNS bytes, emits nothing. The old setMotionTracking name taught setter reflexes and a discarded call was a silent zero-effect failure; this name states what the method is.
setMotionTracking(bool $on): string
prefix(): stringRead-only accessor for the prefix this manager prepends to ids.
mark(string $id, string $content): stringWrap $content with start/end markers for prefix() . $id.
scan(string $rendered, ?int $width = null): stringStrip markers from $rendered, recording each zone's bounding box, and return the cleaned frame ready for the terminal.
get(string $id): ?ZoneLook up a recorded zone.
all(): array
idsAbsentFromFrame(iterable $scannedIds): arrayGeneration-diff prune helper: the registered ids that did not appear among $scannedIds, in registry order (latest recording last).
clear(?string $id = null): voidForget zone state. With no argument, drops every recorded zone (the original clear() shape, kept for back-compat). Pass an $id to drop a single zone — equivalent to the upstream Manager::Clear(id string) overload. Like get(), the $id may be the short or the wire spelling.
close(): voidTear down the manager. Mirrors bubblezone's Manager::Close() — upstream stops the background zoneWorker goroutine here. Our port computes everything synchronously inside scan() so there is no worker to stop, but close() still drops every recorded zone and disables the manager so subsequent mark() / scan() calls become pass-throughs. Idempotent.
anyInBounds(Msg $mouse): ?ZoneThe innermost (smallest-area) recorded zone whose bounds contain $mouse; on equal area the zone the latest scan closed first wins (a re-scanned id takes this scan's close order, not the position of its first-ever recording). This is THE hit rule, shared with the primitive \SugarCraft\Mouse\Scanner::hit() through ZoneGrid, so both layers name the same owner for one painted frame when this Manager holds exactly that frame's zones (it scanned the frame and every id the frame did not paint was cleared via idsAbsentFromFrame()); zones kept from earlier frames can win a cell the frame's Scanner gives to another zone. This registry has no stacking concept — no priority, layer, or modal state — see the overlay contract in README's Zones section before scanning a full-screen modal over a live registry. Returns null if no zone matches (or if the Msg isn't a MouseMsg to begin with — handy when an update() loop routes every Msg here without filtering first).
allInBounds(Msg $mouse): arrayEvery zone whose bounds contain $mouse, ordered innermost first (ascending area; equal areas in registry order — the latest scan's close order for the ids it recorded — matching anyInBounds()). Lets a consumer route a click to ALL owners of a cell — e.g. a container and the button inside it — instead of only the smallest.
zoneAt(int $col, int $row): ?ZonePure-geometry lookup without a Msg: the innermost zone covering cell ($col, $row), 1-based — same area/tie rule as anyInBounds(). Lets consumers resolve what is under the wheel, the caret, or an arbitrary position without fabricating a MouseMsg.
zone(\SugarCraft\Mouse\ZoneId $id): ?ZoneThe zone recorded under a typed id — the \SugarCraft\Mouse\ZoneId spelling of get() (short or wire form, like get()).
lineWidths(): LineWidthCacheThe line-width cache scan() reads and fills.
anyInBoundsAndUpdate(Model $model, Msg $mouse): arrayHit-test $mouse against every recorded zone. If a zone matches, dispatch a MsgZoneInBounds carrying the hit zone + the original Msg through $model->update() and return the resulting pair [Model, ?Cmd]. If nothing matches, dispatch the original Msg verbatim.

ZoneRegistry final class

The per-application home of the state the Zones layer used to keep in statics: the default Manager and the counter behind auto-generated Manager::newPrefix() prefixes.

MethodSummary
static new(): selfA registry whose auto prefixes come from the one process-wide counter.
static isolated(): selfA registry with its own auto prefix counter, starting at 1-. Its prefixes are unique within this registry only: a manager it hands out may share a prefix with one from any other registry.
defaultManager(): ManagerThis registry's shared default manager (un-prefixed), built lazily on first access and kept so zone state persists across mark() → scan() → get() cycles.
setDefaultManager(?Manager $manager): voidReplace the default manager; null drops it so the next defaultManager() builds a fresh enabled one.
newPrefix(string $prefix = ''): ManagerA manager that namespaces every id with a prefix unique within this registry's counter scope (the process for new(), the registry for isolated()). Same contract as Manager::newPrefix(): an empty $prefix auto-generates <n>-; an explicit numeric <n>- prefix is reserved, so a later auto prefix never merges into it.
successor(): selfA new registry with no default manager whose auto prefixes continue after this one's. Zones::setRegistry() resets through it, so a manager built before the reset never shares a prefix with one built after it: Manager::scan() accepts any id that starts with its prefix, and two managers holding 1- would accept each other's zones. A new() registry's successor shares the process counter; an isolated() one's starts from a copy of its counter.
newUnprefixed(): ManagerA fresh un-prefixed manager, independent of the default one.

Zones final class

Package-level facade over a single shared Manager instance.

MethodSummary
static registry(): ZoneRegistryThe process registry the facade and the static Manager::newPrefix() route through, built lazily on first use.
static setRegistry(?ZoneRegistry $registry): voidReplace the process registry; null resets it to an empty default manager while auto prefixes keep counting up, so no process-registry prefix is ever issued twice (ZoneRegistry::successor()). A ZoneRegistry::new() registry draws from the same process-wide counter, so injecting one keeps that guarantee; an injected ZoneRegistry::isolated() registry keeps its own counter, and its managers may share a prefix with another registry's and must not scan each other's frames.
static defaultManager(): ManagerThe shared default Manager of the process registry. Lazily constructed on first access; survives between calls so zone state persists across mark() → scan() → get() cycles.
static setDefaultManager(?Manager $m): voidReplace the shared default manager. Mostly useful in tests (tearDown(): Zones::setDefaultManager(null) flushes state) or when you want every package-level call to route through a pre-configured prefixed manager.
static mark(string $id, string $content): stringMirrors bubblezone's package-level Mark.
static scan(string $rendered, ?int $width = null): stringMirrors bubblezone's Scan. $width clamps zone columns into [1, $width].
static get(string $id): ?ZoneMirrors bubblezone's Get.
static clear(?string $id = null): voidMirrors bubblezone's Clear. Pass an id to drop a single zone; omit to wipe every zone tracked by the default manager.
static close(): voidMirrors bubblezone's Close. After calling this the default manager is disabled (mark / scan become pass-through) and its registry is dropped — Idempotent. WARNING: subsequent package-level calls (Zones::define / Zones::scan / Zones::get …) then pass through silently and hit-tests resolve nothing, i.e. a whole dead UI with no error. Re-arm with Zones::setDefaultManager(null), which lazily builds a fresh enabled default on the next access.
static setEnabled(bool $on): voidMirrors bubblezone's SetEnabled.
static isEnabled(): boolMirrors bubblezone's Enabled.
static newPrefix(string $prefix = ''): ManagerMirrors bubblezone's NewPrefix — but unlike upstream (which returns a string prefix scoped to the default manager), this returns a **fresh prefixed Manager**. Compose multiple components by giving each its own prefixed manager rather than sharing the default. Draws from the process registry's counter, with the same ZoneRegistry::isolated() injection caveat as Manager::newPrefix().
static anyInBounds(Msg $mouse): ?ZoneMirrors bubblezone's AnyInBounds.
static anyInBoundsAndUpdate(Model $model, Msg $mouse): arrayMirrors bubblezone's AnyInBoundsAndUpdate.
